name: Coldseam The Disgraced Arbiter's Exit Suit
description:
Once a Tier-5 judicial robe set, now stripped of insignia and worn into something else entirely. The foundation is a heavy charcoal-and-deep-burgundy brocade longcoat — Spire-quality fabric, unmistakable to anyone who knows — but the corponation seals have been cut out, leaving raw rectangular voids at collar and cuffs. Beneath: a plain white high-collar shirt, hand-pressed, slightly yellowed. Trousers are the original matched brocade, knife-creased out of habit. Shoes are Tier-5 oxfords, re-soled with the Gray Zone rubber — the only practical concession to a new life.

A BCI-port at the temple is exposed, no cosmetic cap. A second port at the base of the skull has been physically sealed with epoxy — something was removed, permanently.
functionality: Spire-grade thermal regulation brocade retains passive warmth, re-soled oxfords provide the Gray Zone-viable traction, exposed BCI port functional, sealed rear port indicates removed implant — nature unknown.
what_it_says: This person fell from the highest tier and kept the coat — either as mourning or as warning.
manufacturer: Coldseam (self-assembled — original Spire garments, the Gray Zone modifications)
price_range: Φ 50 – Φ 120 (current resale; original pieces worth Φ 40,000+)
story_hooks: The sealed skull port contained a judicial memory implant — whatever rulings and secrets were stored there are now inaccessible to everyone, including the wearer.
The raw voids where corponation seals were cut are the exact shape of the Ouroboros Compliance Division insignia — a very specific enemy was made.
A Tier-2 street kid recognizes the brocade pattern from a wanted bulletin; this person presided over a trial that condemned an entire the Gray Zone neighborhood.

physical_description.visual_profile: A figure of deliberate degradation — formal silhouette deliberately unmade. The longcoat drapes with institutional weight, its heavy brocade catching light like old gilt. Collar and cuffs bear rectangular voids where insignia were surgically removed, creating a visual language of erasure. The posture reads as someone who once held authority and now wears that former rank as evidence of loss.
physical_description.fit: Tailored, precise — a Tier-1 cut that refuses to be casual. The coat sits structured at the shoulders, falls to mid-calf with geometric precision. Trousers maintain knife-creases despite the wearer's obvious fall in status. Nothing slouches or relaxes. The fit speaks of muscle memory: this body was trained to move within hierarchy.
physical_description.primary_material: Charcoal-and-deep-burgundy brocade (Spire-quality, unmistakable), heavy weight ballistic-grade backing. Beneath: cotton-synthetic blend for the white shirt. Tier-5 oxford leather, re-soled with industrial shelf rubber.
physical_description.texture: The brocade is tactile — raised damask weave with subtle metallic threading (now dulled), rich and architectural. The cut-out voids reveal raw fabric edges, deliberately unsealed. White shirt is hand-pressed linen-cotton with slight yellowing from time or chemical exposure. Shoes show visible re-sole scarring where shelf rubber has been grafted onto original leather uppers.
physical_description.color_scheme: Charcoal and deep burgundy brocade (the coat's foundation — a color combination that screams Spire judicial authority). Pure white high-collar shirt, yellowed to ivory at edges and collar. Black trousers. Weathered tan-to-grey oxfords with crude black rubber soles.
physical_description.closures: Magnetic snaps (Spire-grade, still functional) along the coat front, though one upper snap is visibly corroded. High-collar shirt uses friction-fit metal studs, slightly oxidized. Trousers are traditional button-fly with a single worn brass button.
distinctive_features: Rectangular voids cut from collar and cuffs — removed insignia leave raw edges
Exposed BCI port at temple, no cosmetic cap or cover
Second port at base of skull sealed shut with dark epoxy resin — deliberate permanent closure
Hand-pressed white shirt with visible yellowing
Knife-creased trousers maintained despite tier-5 circumstances
Shelf rubber grafted directly onto original Spire oxford leather
Slight chemical discoloration on inner coat cuffs
One corroded magnetic snap near coat neckline
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier-1 garment worn by someone now Tier-5 — the contradiction is the statement. The Spire brocade is recognizable wealth. The voids and re-sold shoes are recognizable exile.
physical_description.cultural_context: A disgraced judicial arbiter. Someone who made a choice (or was forced) to sever ties to the Spire authority structure. The exposed BCI ports suggest forced de-authentication or voluntary self-sabotage. The sealed port at the base of skull indicates something was removed — possibly a loyalty override, a compliance chip, or access credentials. Wearing this outfit is a form of testimony: *I was someone. I chose to stop being.*
physical_description.condition_typical: Broken-in and deliberate. Not neglected — the precision of the knife-creases and hand-pressing suggests ritual maintenance. But weathered by use and time. The voids are fresh enough to show raw threads, but old enough that the wearer has grown accustomed to them. This is someone who has integrated their disgrace into their appearance.
